scenario_category: claims with different levels of corroboration
description: A single product-recall event contains one well-corroborated claim, one consensus claim, and one thinly sourced claim that should not be elevated to the same confidence level.

event.title: Household appliance recall announced
event.description: A manufacturer recalls a kitchen appliance; some details are well-confirmed, others are only lightly sourced.

articles.title: Brightline Appliances recalls 220,000 units of countertop ovens
articles.summary: Confirmed via company statement: the recall covers 220,000 units and is voluntary.
articles.raw_content: Brightline Appliances announced a voluntary recall of approximately 220,000 countertop ovens due to a fire risk in the heating element. The company said the recall is voluntary and customers can receive a full refund or replacement. The recall was confirmed in a company press release.

articles.title: Brightline confirms 220,000-unit voluntary recall
articles.summary: Second outlet confirms the same recall scope and voluntary nature via the same company statement.
articles.raw_content: Confirming Brightline Appliances' press release, this outlet verified the recall covers 220,000 countertop ovens and is voluntary, with refund or replacement options offered to affected customers.

articles.title: Sources say recall driven by pending injury lawsuit, company has not confirmed
articles.summary: A single outlet, citing an anonymous source, claims the recall was prompted by a specific lawsuit; not corroborated or confirmed by the company.
articles.raw_content: According to a single person described as familiar with internal discussions, the recall decision was driven in part by a pending lawsuit alleging a burn injury from one of the ovens. Brightline Appliances has not confirmed this account, and no other outlet has corroborated it. The person did not provide details about the lawsuit.

must_preserve_facts: The recall covers approximately 220,000 units and is voluntary (confirmed by company statement and two outlets)
The claim that a specific lawsuit drove the recall decision comes from a single anonymous source and has not been confirmed by the company or corroborated elsewhere
must_not_invent: Specific details of the alleged lawsuit (none are given in the source)
Confirmation of the lawsuit claim by the company (explicitly not confirmed)
known_ambiguities: The recall scope/voluntary-nature claim (articles 91, 92) is well-corroborated and should likely be tagged 'consensus'. The lawsuit-motivation claim (article 93) is thinly and anonymously sourced with no corroboration and should be tagged 'unconfirmed', not elevated to the same confidence level as the recall-scope claim just because both appear in the same event.
validation_notes: Tests that a model applies different status values ('consensus' vs 'unconfirmed') to different claims WITHIN the same event rather than assigning a single uniform confidence level to everything reported about this event.
